messages:
anya: Heads-up — during month-close I noticed AcmeCorp (acct 1234) dashboard total != invoice. Dashboard shows 2,340,512 tokens, invoice INV-2024-11-30 shows 2,210,192. Tier on invoice = Pro (upgrade mid-window). Screenshot: https://redwood.share/snap/abc123 :eyes:

matt: Thanks. Can you paste the invoice id + dashboard snapshot id? I'll pull ledger and invoice lines.

anya: Invoice INV-2024-11-30, dashboard snapshot dsp-20241130-3. Diff = 130,320 tokens. Customer is on Standard -> Pro upgrade on 2024-11-20 (mid-billing-window).

jia: Ping @billing-bot for generation metadata and any webhook errors around invoice creation. Also: did we run any backfill or reingestion jobs for that account last week?

billing-bot: Invoice INV-2024-11-30 generated at 2024-12-01T02:03:12Z. Applied plan: Pro (effective 2024-11-20T14:00:00Z). Usage window: 2024-11-01T00:00:00Z -> 2024-11-30T23:59:59Z. No webhook failures recorded for invoice creation.

leo: Quick thought — dashboard shows raw metering events, invoice applies proration + plan attribution rules. But the token delta looks exactly like an 'overage' line I see in the invoice detail. Are there duped metering events?

matt: On initial glance I see an invoice line: "pro_overage" quantity 130,320 tokens. That matches the difference. We need to know whether those tokens were actually billed (correct) or if the dashboard double-counted earlier.

anya: Running a metering export now for acct 1234 (11/01 -> 11/30). Command: ``./internal/tools/meter-export --acct 1234 --start 2024-11-01 --end 2024-11-30 > /tmp/acme-meters.ndjson``. Will paste head output when done.

(anya uploads)
```
{ "request_id": "r-ff1", "tokens": 512, "ingest_ts": "2024-11-19T23:59:59Z" }
{ "request_id": "r-ff1", "tokens": 512, "ingest_ts": "2024-11-20T00:00:05Z" }
{ "request_id": "r-ff2", "tokens": 2048, "ingest_ts": "2024-11-21T12:10:03Z" }
```

jia: Those first two look suspicious — same request_id r-ff1 twice (23:59:59 vs 00:00:05) across the upgrade boundary. That smells like a retry/backfill that wasn't deduped by the dashboard snapshot. Can you run a quick dedupe-check query?

leo: Query snippet: ``SELECT request_id, count(*) FROM meter_events WHERE account_id=1234 AND ingest_ts BETWEEN '2024-11-01' AND '2024-11-30' GROUP BY request_id HAVING count(*) > 1 LIMIT 10;``

anya: Ran it — result: ``r-ff1: 2, r-abc9: 2, r-zz12: 3``. Total duplicated token sum = 130,320 tokens.

claire-finance: If duplicated events explain the delta, invoice likely billed correctly (invoice dedup logic used event fingerprints + billing window) OR we might have double-billed if invoice pipeline didn't dedupe. Which pipeline dedup do we trust?

jia: Two separate systems: dashboard UI dedupes on first-seen ingest_ts and request_id fingerprint; billing pipeline dedupes using hashed event_id + backfill flags. Looks like some events were retried with new ingest_ts but same request_id, which our dashboard did not collapse. Billing pipeline collapsed correctly, hence invoice smaller.

matt: So root cause hypothesis: reingestion/backfill created duplicate meter events with new ingest_ts after plan upgrade; dashboard snapshot counted both, billing pipeline deduped, invoice is correct.

anya: Steps to repro for engineering ops: 1) Replay request_id r-ff1 with old ingest ts then reingest with new ingest ts across the plan-change boundary; 2) snapshot dashboard counts; 3) run billing dedupe and compare. I can share ndjson sample.

jia: Excellent — can you attach a minimal repro ndjson? Also include the SDK client version and whether the customer used bulk ingest vs live intake. That affects dedupe semantics.

anya: Attached sample (3 events) and customer uses ingestion v1.3.2 (bulk). Repro steps: ``curl -X POST /meter -d @sample.json --header 'x-account:1234'`` then re-post same sample with slight timestamp offset. Dashboard increments twice, billing pipeline de-dupes.

leo: Short-term mitigation: We can add a dashboard-side dedupe pass for the month-close snapshot (id dsp-20241130-3) to collapse on request_id before reporting. That should align UI with invoice. Ops work needed.

claire-finance: If ops can produce a corrected snapshot, we'll hold off issuing a credit until we confirm. Customer is flagged as high-touch; don't adjust invoice without confirmation.

matt: Action items: (1) eng (jia) validate dedupe semantics and produce corrected snapshot or a reconciliation diff; (2) ops (anya/leo) run dashboard dedupe pass for dsp-20241130-3 and share CSV; (3) finance (claire/matt) hold invoice reconciliation with Acme until we confirm.

jia: I'll run a quick script to simulate dedupe and produce reconciled token totals. ETA 45m.

anya: Thanks — will keep thread updated. :thumbsup:

(45m later)
jia: Reconciled snapshot attached. After collapsing on request_id, dashboard total = 2,210,192 tokens which matches invoice. Root cause: duplicated meter events from bulk reingest that produced new ingest_ts; dashboard snapshot didn't collapse by request_id at that time.

claire-finance: Good — we'll notify Acme that invoice stands but we'll add an explanation note. Also recommend we add an automated reconciliation check on month-close to catch these deltas earlier.

leo: Filed infra issue https://redwood.issues/INF-6543 to add dashboard dedupe at snapshot time and a reconciliation alert.

anya: Closing loop with customer now. Thanks all. :tada:
